prompt: John would like to own his own electronics business. He has set aside some money for investment but has very little time for the day-to-day operations of a business. What type of business ownership would you recommend?
explanation: Corporation. Corporation ownership permits ownership by simply buying shares of stock. Sole proprietorship is a form of ownership that requires owner participation. General partnership is designed to combine the capital, experience, and abilities of two or more people. Close corporations do not offer their shares for sale to the general public.

prompt: A recommended way to find out why the caller has phoned your electronics business is to
choices: ask the caller, "What did you want?"
wait for the caller to ask questions.
ask the caller, "How may I help you?"
answer promptly with a friendly greeting.
explanation: Ask the caller, "How may I help you?" This question requires callers to identify the purpose of their calls. It is courteous, since you cannot provide assistance until you know what is needed. Asking, "What did you want?" sounds abrupt and impolite. Waiting for callers to ask questions would waste your time and that of the caller's. Answering promptly with a friendly greeting is a guideline for giving good telephone service, but would not identify the purpose of the call.

prompt: What is the main form of written communication between companies?
explanation: Business letters. Business letters are the most common form of written communication used by businesses to exchange information with other organizations or with customers. Memorandums are informal letters or notes between a company's employees. They are the main form of written communication within a business. Telephone calls and meetings are not forms of written communication.

prompt: What information should a technical equipment manufacturer's employees avoid sharing with their coworkers?
explanation: Current salary. Certain information is considered personal and confidential and should not be shared with coworkers. An employee's salary is confidential information between the business and the employee and should not be divulged to others. Inventory policy, promotional ideas, and operating hours are types of information that usually are available to all employees.

prompt: Determine whether the following statement is true or false: Distribution can affect the success of a technical company's products.
choices: True, products must be at the right place at the right time.
True, effective distribution decreases capital investment.
False, distribution is only one small part of marketing.
False, quality products will succeed regardless of distribution.
explanation: True, products must be at the right place at the right time. Distribution methods are as important to the success of products as the products themselves. Even good products can fail if they are not where customers can purchase them or are not at the business when the customer needs them. Capital investment is not reduced by effective distribution. Distribution is one part of marketing, but it has become increasingly important, and its costs make up about half of total marketing costs.

prompt: Technological advances that allow music to be sent and received over the Internet have moved the music industry from physical distribution to __________ distribution.
explanation: Digital. Digital technology allows music to be downloaded over the Internet and saved to disk, thereby eliminating intermediaries, cutting cycle time, and moving the music industry away from traditional physical distribution methods. Video and virtual usually refer to image information, and analogue is used in wireless telephone communication.

prompt: Why is it important for an electronics store chain to coordinate distribution with its promotional activities?
choices: To offer products at extremely low prices
To spend money on warehousing surplus products
To make sure that products are available on time
To select the most efficient transportation form
explanation: To make sure that products are available on time. An electronics store chain should plan promotional activities in advance because it needs to develop advertising, print coupons, schedule special sales, and organize events to promote the products. If the products are not available during the promotion, customers will be unable to purchase them, and the promotion will be ineffective. Therefore, it is important for an electronics store chain to coordinate distribution with their promotional activities to make sure that the products are available when advertised. An electronics store chain does not coordinate distribution with promotional activities in order to offer products at extremely low prices, spend money on warehousing, or select the most efficient transportation form.

prompt: One of the advantages to a technical business of using independent representatives to sell its products to intermediaries is that the representatives are
choices: allowed to call on many businesses.
explanation: Not on the business's payroll. Independent representatives are channel members who sell the products of several businesses or manufacturers. They often represent several businesses that sell related, but noncompeting, products. The advantage to the business of using independent representatives to sell products is that the representatives are paid on a commission basis. When they sell products, they are paid a certain percentage of the sale price as a commission. The representatives are not on the technical business's payroll, which saves the technical business money because it pays a commission only on actual sales and does not have the added expense of benefits or salaries. Independent representatives are not necessarily more qualified than other salespeople. They are required to follow any selling regulations that apply. All salespeople, including independent representatives, are allowed to call on any business that might be a potential customer.

prompt: Which of the following is an example of a capital good:
explanation: Factory. Capital goods are manufactured or constructed items used to produce goods and services. This includes the buildings in which production takes place. A salesperson is a human resource. Trees and minerals are natural resources.

prompt: Which business activity ensures that an electronics parts company will have goods to sell?
explanation: Production. Production is the creation of goods and services from economic resources. Without production, there would be no need for the other business activities as the electronics parts company would have nothing to sell. Finance is the process of obtaining funds and using them to achieve the goals of the business. Management is the process of coordinating resources in order to accomplish an organization's goals. Promotion is a marketing function that communicates information about goods, services, images, and/or ideas to achieve a desired outcome.

prompt: A country that has a socialistic command economic system is
explanation: Great Britain. Socialism is a modified command economic system in which government owns the basic means of production but there is private ownership of businesses as well. Socialism is characterized by freedom of choice, limited competition, high taxes, some government control, and welfare programs for citizens. Japan, Switzerland, and the United States have capitalistic economic systems.

prompt: Net profit is money left after a business has paid
choices: the cost of goods for resale.
explanation: All of its expenses. These would include salaries; the costs of running the business, known as operating expenses; and the cost of goods.

prompt: What aspect of collective bargaining signals the successful end of negotiations?
choices: Management and union leaders have completed their research on the issues.
Union leaders and management have met to present their demands.
Management and union leaders have reached a tentative agreement.
A mediator has clarified the issues and offered suggestions to both sides.
explanation: Management and union leaders have reached a tentative agreement. Both sides have agreed on the terms and working conditions; however, final approval has not been given by union members. Management and union leaders complete their research on the issues during the initial step of collective bargaining when they are preparing for negotiations. A mediator would clarify the issues and offer suggestions during the bargaining sessions when the union leaders and management meet to present their demands.

prompt: Because the economy was experiencing a rapid inflation rate and consumer spending fell, the NOP Appliance Manufacturing Company had to
explanation: Reduce its outputs. Inflation refers to the rise in prices within an economic system. When inflation levels are high, the economy often experiences a period of contraction. Consumer purchasing power decreases, which often reduces the demand for goods and services. To stay in business, the NOP Appliance Manufacturing Company might reduce outputs (e.g., production, personnel) because of a lower demand for its products. When outputs decrease, the inputs also decrease. Interest rates are often low during an economic expansion, which means it costs less to obtain loans for large purchases (e.g., equipment).

prompt: Goods and services purchased from other nations are referred to as
explanation: Imports. Imports are items that are purchased from other countries. Reasons that a country imports goods are because the items are not available in the homeland, are in short supply, or are priced more competitively in other countries. Exports are goods and services sold by businesses and industries to individuals, manufacturers, or governments in other countries. International trade is the buying and selling of goods and services between nations. Domestic trade is the buying and selling of goods and services within a country.

prompt: What is often the result of positive customer/client relations?
explanation: Repeat business. Salespeople who develop positive relationships with customers usually are able to maintain those customers over a period of time. The benefit of having positive customer relationships is repeat business. Salespeople know that it is more time consuming and expensive to attract new customers than it is to keep existing customers. Therefore, salespeople try to build good relationships with their customers in order to keep their business. Positive customer/client relations do not result in more competition, additional stress, or increased training.

prompt: As an employee with a small electronics firm, Jim believes that he is better than his coworkers because he has had some college classes and they have not. Jim's coworkers dislike his __________ attitude.
explanation: Superior. Conceited, arrogant, and snobbish are other terms frequently used to describe people with a superior attitude toward others. Such immature people frequently try to dominate others when they are in a group setting. People with a positive attitude look on the bright side of things. Aggressive people ignore the rights of and exploit others in order to achieve personal goals.

prompt: Appliance store employees can generally identify difficult customers
explanation: During their initial contact. Most appliance store employees learn a lot about customers during their first conversation with the customers by listening, observing, and questioning the customers. This should not include asking personal questions. The way in which customers dress or speak would not indicate whether they will be difficult to help.

prompt: When trying to resolve a dispute raised by a customer, it is important for a cellular phone salesperson to
explanation: Offer several options. When trying to resolve a dispute raised by a customer, a cellular phone salesperson should try to find out what the customer really wants and offer several options. In most cases, there is more than one way to solve the problem, and providing several solutions will allow customers to chose the one that best meets their needs. For example, some customers may prefer a refund while others will be satisfied with an exchange. Merely restating company policy will not resolve a dispute. Salespeople do not provide written explanations and should not ask personal questions.

prompt: When customers buy on credit, the money owed the electronics store by the customers is part of the store's
explanation: Accounts receivable. Accounts receivable are monies owed to an electronics store by its customers. Whenever a customer makes a credit purchase, s/he owes the electronics store or the credit-card company a debt. Cash receipts are income in the form of currency or coins. Current liabilities are debts that must be paid within a year. Accounts payable are debts owed by the electronics store.

prompt: What type of money is recorded in the cash receipts column of a cash flow statement?
explanation: Collected. Only collected money is recorded under cash receipts. For example, if a business expects to make $5,000 from cash sales and $2,000 from credit sales, it records only the $5,000 in the cash receipts column. The $2,000 in credit sales is referred to as accounts receivable and should not be recorded until it is actually collected, otherwise the business will appear to have more money on hand than it actually does. Expenses are listed in the cash payments column rather than in the cash receipts column.

prompt: Which of the following is a function of an operating budget:
explanation: To control expenditures. A budget is an estimate of what income and expenses will be for a specific period of time. One of the main functions of an operating budget is to control expenditures so that businesses do not spend more money than they have available. Recording financial data is an accounting function. Operating budgets do not monitor accounting or regulate inflation.

prompt: In which of the following situations might a television manufacturer be able to increase the amount of cash inflow on a monthly basis:
choices: Taking a 2% discount for paying within 90 days
Offering a 2% discount within 20 days of invoice date
Delaying paying purchases on account for 30 days
Charging 2% interest on past due accounts
explanation: Offering a 2% discount within 20 days of invoice date. Television manufacturers often take actions to increase their monthly cash inflow after analyzing current cash flow patterns. One action that a television manufacturer might take is to offer 2% discounts to customers who pay within 20 days of the invoice date. The discount encourages customers to pay promptly, which improves the television manufacturer's cash inflow. Taking a 2% discount and delaying payment on accounts payable might improve the television manufacturer's cash outflow rather than its cash inflow. Charging interest on past due accounts will not increase monthly cash inflow because customers are delinquent in making payments.

prompt: Which of the following is a disadvantage of an hourly wage plan for compensating employees:
choices: There is a large amount of clerical work involved.
The employee knows how much s/he will receive each time.
No immediate incentive for extra effort or good work is offered.
explanation: No immediate incentive for extra effort or good work is offered. The employee is paid based on hours worked, not productivity. A raise may be an incentive for hard work, but it is long term, rather than immediate. Profit-sharing plans may be offered by management under any pay plan. Advantages of the hourly wage plan include predictability of wages and less clerical work.

prompt: Which of the following tests would be used to evaluate a job applicant's ability to learn a particular kind of job:
explanation: Aptitude. An aptitude test is designed to measure a person's natural ability in a particular discipline. It indicates whether a person can be trained to do a job. A work sample would require an applicant to perform an aspect of a job as a test of his/her current skills. A polygraph test is used to determine an applicant's truthfulness, and polygraph testing is restricted or forbidden in some states. A personality test measures an applicant's motivation rather than job skills or ability.

prompt: To train a customer service representative for the XYZ Telecommunications Company's telemarketing department, the best method would be __________training.
explanation: Laboratory. This training is conducted by company instructors in facilities that simulate on-the-job working conditions. On-the-job training places a new employee under close supervision until she is skilled enough to do the job alone. It slows production while the new employee learns. Apprenticeship training requires a worker to function as an assistant for several years in order to become skilled. It is frequently used in skilled trades. Supervisory training programs are designed to improve the leadership and management skills of supervisors.

prompt: A business equipment company should evaluate the effectiveness of its training and development programs in order to
choices: determine whether new hires are needed.
know whether the expense was worthwhile.
identify the population to be served.
explanation: Know whether the expense was worthwhile. A business equipment company needs to evaluate the outcome of its training and development programs in order to know whether the results were worth the time and money that were spent. Evaluating the program's effectiveness will not reduce future training and development needs since these needs are generally ongoing. Evaluation also does not determine the need for new hires. The identification of the population to be served occurs when training and development needs are prioritized.

prompt: The XYZ Company is interested in developing, producing, and selling a new electronics product. Before it does so, the company spends six months conducting marketing research. What are the primary advantages of this course of action?
choices: To predict trends and provide information to customers
To increase costs and determine consumer dislikes
To determine customer preferences and minimize losses
To delay the production process and increase labor costs
explanation: To determine customer preferences and minimize losses. Businesses obtain marketing information in order to develop a product that customers want and need. By doing research, companies obtain marketing information that helps them to minimize the losses that may occur from introducing a product that customers do not want. Businesses do not conduct marketing research to increase costs, although they may identify consumer dislikes. The goal is not to delay production or increase labor costs. Marketing research may identify trends, but it is not intended to provide information to customers.

prompt: A marketing-information management system should meet the requirements of the
explanation: Individual business. A marketing-information management system is valuable if it can meet the needs of the individual business by providing information so that appropriate decisions can be made. The marketing researcher, the salesperson, and computer operator are individuals who are employed by the individual business and can be internal sources of information for the system.

prompt: Finding out why people in a community spend money on a given product is an example of
explanation: Qualitative research. The aim of qualitative research is to explore and understand the attitudes, opinions, feelings, and behaviors of individuals or a group of individuals. In quantitative research, the aim is to determine the relationship between one thing (an independent variable) and another (a dependent or outcome variable) in a population. Interviewing is a method of qualitative research, while gathering demographic information is a form of quantitative research.

prompt: Why do many businesses use computer technology to manage marketing information?
choices: To send direct-mail pieces to customers
To merge a variety of data into one database
To develop software that fits a specific need
explanation: To merge a variety of data into one database. Businesses often obtain information about customers from a variety of sources such as questionnaires, warranty cards, or sweepstakes entries. All of this information is valuable if the businesses are able to merge it into a database that is easily accessible. A business's customer database might include information about name, address, types of recent purchases, dollar amounts spent, general interests, income, brand preferences, etc. Businesses use the merged database to target specific customers or identify trends in order to remain competitive. Businesses might purchase software in order to prepare questionnaires or direct-mail pieces that will be sent to customers, but not to manage marketing information.

prompt: How can an electronics distributor use its sales force to determine the reasons for customer attrition?
choices: Increase advertising to attract new customers
Use an online database to track the activities of the sales representatives
Have sales representatives encourage customers to visit the company web site
Require sales representatives to submit lost-business reports on each lost customer
explanation: Require sales representatives to submit lost-business reports on each lost customer. Requiring sales representatives to submit lost-business reports on each lost customer would allow the company to learn the reasons customers are leaving and to determine areas where improvements are needed. Increasing advertising and using an online database are not ways of using the sales force. Asking customers to visit the web site will not obtain the needed information.

prompt: Marketing research can affect an electronics store's marketing mix by providing information about what competitors charge for their goods and services, which will influence the __________ decision.
explanation: Price. The price decision involves determining the amount of money marketers will ask in exchange for their products. In order to be successful, an electronics store must keep its prices in line with competitors' prices. The place decision involves getting products in the right place at the right time. The product decision involves selecting the goods, services, or ideas that the electronics store will sell. The promotion decision involves selecting the type of communications that will be used to provide information about the electronics store's goods, services, images, and/or ideas to achieve a desired outcome.

prompt: Objectives that technical businesses want to attain are known as
explanation: Goals. To be successful, technical businesses must have goals and objectives—things that they want to attain. Examples of goals are to reduce costs, to increase sales, to change an image, etc. Strategies are the plans of action for achieving goals and objectives. Tactics are the specific actions to be used to carry out strategies. Marketing mixes are the combination of the elements of marketing.

prompt: Market segmentation can benefit a cellular telephone company by helping it to
explanation: Market products efficiently. Market segmentation is the division of a total market into smaller, more specific groups. This is accomplished by identifying those persons who will be the most likely customers for a product based upon their similar characteristics and needs. A cellular telephone company that wants to appeal to the general population uses mass marketing. Operational changes are changes in the way a business is set up or operates (e.g., remodeling or expanding parking). The use of market segmentation is more likely to increase, rather than reduce, production costs.

prompt: Why is it important for telecommunication businesses to analyze the competition on a regular basis?
choices: To compete on an ethical basis
explanation: To determine ways to compete. Telecommunication businesses need to analyze the competition on a regular basis in order to understand their competitors and to develop ways to effectively compete in the marketplace. The competitive environment changes constantly. Therefore, telecommunication businesses must keep up to date with what their competitors are doing in order to remain successful. Telecommunication businesses do not analyze the competition in order to eliminate competitors, understand laws regulating competition, or compete on an ethical basis.

prompt: Which of the following is an internal strength that a business equipment manufacturer might identify during a SWOT analysis:
explanation: Financial resources. A SWOT analysis is the systematic evaluation of a business's internal strengths and weaknesses and external opportunities and threats. SWOT stands for strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats. One of the internal strengths that a SWOT analysis might identify is a business's financial resources. Having sufficient financial resources to develop new products and services is an internal strength that a business can use to grow and prosper. Extensive regulations are an external threat, while limited competition is an external opportunity. Increased expenses are an internal weakness.

prompt: An important step in the process of developing a marketing plan involves selecting the
explanation: Target market. The target market is the group of consumers on whom the business focuses its marketing efforts. An important part of developing a marketing plan involves selecting the target market because the purpose of the marketing plan is to establish procedures or strategies for attracting those target customers. A business needs to know which customers it is trying to reach in order to make decisions about how to reach them. Businesses often conduct research in order to gather important information before starting to develop a marketing plan. Once a marketing plan has been developed, a business might select a distribution agent and a sales force.

prompt: A business equipment company comparing and evaluating the actual sales in one territory with the goals for that territory is an example of a(n)
explanation: Sales analysis. When a business equipment company compares and evaluates actual sales in a territory with the goals for that territory, it is conducting a sales analysis. The purpose of a sales analysis is to measure performance in order to make adjustments in the marketing plan, if necessary. For example, if a business equipment company fails to achieve its sales goal, it knows that it must make changes in order to increase sales. Part of a sales analysis also involves trying to identify the reasons for not making goal. A territory quota is the sales, or performance, goal the territory is expected to meet. Comparing actual sales with goals does not involve reviewing expenses.

prompt: Identify the term that best represents marketing's role in society.
explanation: Problem solver. Of the options given, "problem solver" is the term that best represents marketing's role in society. Marketing connects producers to customers by solving customers' problems. Pioneers lead and peacemakers make peace — with or without being involved in marketing or its role in society.

prompt: Which of the following illustrates a trend in professional technical selling:
explanation: Business intelligence systems. These are computer programs that take customer information, product costs, and sales figures to make the information useful to the business. Telemarketing, point-of-purchase displays, and frequent-user programs are not used in professional technical selling, due to the nature of the products sold.

prompt: Which of the following is information about employees that technical businesses are required by law to maintain:
explanation: Identification numbers. Technical businesses are required by law to maintain certain information about their employees, such as their identification numbers. These numbers might be Social Security numbers and employee ID numbers that clearly identify each employee. Technical businesses use these numbers when reporting wage and salary information to the government for tax purposes. Many technical businesses maintain data about their employees' nearest relatives, educational histories, and references, but this information is not required by law.

prompt: Which of the following is a true statement about safety hazards in the workplace:
choices: Poor housekeeping can cause safety hazards.
Safety hazards are obvious to most people.
Safety hazards are the same for most businesses.
Equipment that needs repair is not a safety hazard.
explanation: Poor housekeeping can cause safety hazards. Cluttered areas of the workplace can create safety hazards. For example, people can trip over items lying on the floor, slip on liquids that have been spilled, or be injured when poorly-stacked containers fall over. Safety hazards differ according to the kind of business. Equipment that needs repair may have loose parts or malfunction in a way that would injure workers. Safety hazards are not obvious to most people unless they have been taught to recognize them.

prompt: Electronics store employees who falsify payroll records or punch time cards for other employees are contributing to
explanation: Employee theft. Falsifying payroll records or punching time cards for coworkers who are not working are examples of employee theft because the electronics store is paying wages to people who are not performing their job duties. Shoplifting occurs when a customer steals merchandise. Tax fraud involves reporting false tax information to the government. Pilferage is stealing by hiding merchandise in shopping bags or any concealed places.

prompt: What industrial purchasing structure exists when authority for all purchasing activities, regardless of geographic location, lies with one department or individual?
explanation: Centralized. This type of structure is efficient and profitable for organizations with a single production facility. Decentralized purchasing structures exist when each department performs its own purchasing activities. A departmentalized purchasing structure is a combination of centralized and decentralized purchasing. The warehouse-and-requisition plan is a type of centralized retail buying in which central buying arranges for an initial assortment of merchandise to be shipped to individual stores.

prompt: Production is often called a conversion process because it
explanation: Turns resources into products. Production is the process or activity of producing goods or services wanted by consumers. Production takes the business's resources (inputs) and turns them into salable products (outputs). If the products produced make a profit for the business, this could change business failure to success, but that is not the reason production is called a conversion process. Product utility is usefulness or the capability of satisfying consumers' needs, which is a desirable result of the production process.

prompt: In order to focus on important activities, what should employees do once they have identified their job-related objectives?
explanation: Put them in writing. Once employees have identified their job-related objectives, they should write them down. Putting their objectives in writing will help employees to focus their attention on important activities, and to decide which ones should be accomplished first. Employees write down their job-related objectives in order to help them manage their time. Employees do not need to share their objectives with their associates, send their objectives to managers, or ask for assistance.

prompt: Telecommunication businesses that control expenses can carry out research and development activities because they have more
explanation: Profits. Profit is the monetary reward a business owner receives for taking the risk of investing in business. Telecommunication businesses need profits, the money left after all expenses are paid, in order to carry out research and development activities. These activities are necessary for telecommunication businesses to develop new or improved goods that help them compete with others. Telecommunication businesses of any size can work on controlling expenses; it does not take more employees to do this. Subsidies are financial assistance given to businesses or individuals by the government. Quotas are specific goals to be met.

prompt: A large wholesale business has gross sales of $2,800,000, and its delivery expense amounted to 4.3% of gross sales. How much could the business save if it reduced that figure to 4%?
explanation: $8,400. To find the dollar amount for current delivery expenses, multiply gross sales by the percentage of gross sales ($2,800,000 x 4.3% or .043 = $120,400). Then, multiply gross sales by the reduced percentage ($2,800,000 x 4% or .04 = $112,000). Subtract this figure from the current delivery expense to determine the possible savings ($120,400 - $112,000 = $8,400).

prompt: Which of the following is considered a "stepping stone" toward achieving a specific objective:
explanation: Subgoal. A subgoal is a lesser goal that must be achieved in order to reach the main goal. A want is a desire. A long-term goal is one that takes more than a year to achieve. Few, if any, people have unlimited resources but must use the resources available to them in order to achieve their goals.

prompt: When preparing letters of application for jobs, individuals who have very little work experience should stress their
explanation: Education. Individuals should stress their education and achievements at school when they have very little work experience. Prospective employers are interested in finding out if the applicants have the training and ability to perform well on the job. If applicants explain that they have the educational background to do the work, prospective employers are often willing to interview them. Information about references is listed in a resume. Letters of application usually do not contain information about an individual's personality or activities unless those activities relate directly to the job.

prompt: Which of the following is perhaps the most valuable benefit professional organizations provide to their members:
choices: Training in math and accounting, because being a successful technical salesperson depends heavily on having expertise in these areas.
Resume preparation, since experts recommend that technical sales professionals, more than any other group, always be ready to look for a job.
Dress-for-success workshops, since looking the part of the knowledgeable professional is especially critical for success in technical sales.
Networking with colleagues, since this is recommended as an important source of prospects, idea sharing, and support.
explanation: Networking with colleagues, since this is recommended as an important source of prospects, idea sharing, and support. Particularly in technical sales, where salespeople work independently, networking through professional organizations is an extremely important, necessary activity. Networking offers an opportunity to exchange ideas, as well as give and receive support. Consultants also recommend networking as an effective technique for prospecting for new business. Salespeople may acquire tips on resume preparation through professional organizations, but this is probably not one of the primary benefits provided. Experts recommend that everyone-not only technical sales professionals-always keep their resumes updated. Services provided by professional organizations do not generally include dress-for-success workshops or training in math and accounting. Everyone, including technical salespeople, needs to present a professional appearance. Although math and accounting are valuable skills, technical salespeople can be successful without expertise in accounting.

prompt: Raising the prices of electronic products to be exported to offset the expenses of transportation, taxes, and tariffs is
explanation: Ethical and legal. It is not illegal or unethical to raise prices to recoup expenses of selling products abroad as long as the price increase does not exceed the additional costs.

prompt: Which of the following is an example of computer technology that is affecting the way some electronics stores mark prices on their products:
choices: POS terminals that prepare sales reports
explanation: Software that generates product tags. Marking prices on goods is a major consideration for most electronics stores and it is also costly. Advances in computer technology have allowed for the development of certain types of software, which enable electronics stores to use their own computers to generate a variety of product tags and labels that include price information. Electronics stores can create labels that are unique to their operations and include the kind of information that is most useful to them. The software also allows electronics stores to print new price tags whenever necessary. Electronics stores do not use POS terminals, scanners, and ATM machines to mark prices on products.

prompt: A warranty which covers the entire product is known as a(n) __________ warranty.
explanation: Full. A full warranty is not limited to certain aspects of the product but covers the entire product. A warranty concerning the quality of the product that is written or expressed verbally is an express warranty. A limited warranty does not contain the provisions of a full warranty—it may cover only certain repairs or specific parts. An implied warranty is understood by the consumer and the seller that the product will perform as expected.

prompt: Why might an electronics company decide to decrease the prices of its products?
explanation: To reach a different market. Electronics businesses sometimes make changes in their products or product lines that might involve decreasing prices. One reason that an electronics company decreases its prices is to try to appeal to a different market. They may alter product quality in order to reduce prices and appeal to a different, low-priced market. Electronics companies expand their product mix in order to offer complementary goods and provide a wider variety. Electronics companies may contract their product mix in order to satisfy legal liabilities.

prompt: Which of the following bundling strategies is being used when a buyer locates a complete collector's edition set and is willing to pay more for the set than if the individual pieces were found and purchased separately:
explanation: Premium. Premium bundling occurs when the products purchased in bundle formats are more expensive than if purchased separately, such as when a buyer sees value added as a time-saving feature or if the bundle includes a limited distribution item. Add-on bundling occurs when products are only sold if a lead product is purchased. Pure bundling occurs when products are available only as a bundle. Mixed bundling means that products are available separately or in bundle fashion.

prompt: All the different items that a business sells is the business's product
explanation: Mix. Product mix is the particular assortment of goods and services that a business offers in order to meet its market's needs and its company's goals. Therefore, all the different items that a business sells are the business's product mix. Product line is a group of related product items. Product width is the number of different product lines that a business sells. Product depth is the number of items in each product line.

prompt: An existing business equipment company might determine the appropriate services to add to its product mix by
explanation: Asking its customers. To improve or expand its product mix, a business equipment company might ask its existing customer base about their needs, wants, and level of current satisfaction with the products. The information can be used to identify additional services that can satisfy the customers' needs and enhance their experiences with the business. A business equipment company buys the supplies (e.g., goods, services) that it needs to run the business from its vendors. Obtaining information or feedback from its vendors does not necessarily help the business equipment company in determining which service options it should provide its customers. A target market is a particular group of customers that a business seeks to attract. An existing business equipment company has already identified its target markets and therefore, does not need to go through the process again. A sales forecast is a prediction of future sales over a specific period of time. Although sales forecasts can influence the types and levels of services a business equipment company offers, they are not developed for the purpose of determining the services.

prompt: A high-definition television manufacturer that says it tries harder because its products are not number one is using product positioning to
explanation: Compete. A high-definition television manufacturer might position its products to compete successfully with other, similar products. By saying that it tries harder because its products are not number one, the manufacturer is positioning its products to compete. The goal is to make the product stand out and draw attention to the fact that, although the product is the same as competitors' products, the high-definition television manufacturer will try harder to satisfy customers. A high-definition television manufacturer that says it tries harder to satisfy its customers' needs is not using product positioning to motivate, organize, or upgrade.

prompt: When customers will not accept a substitute for a brand they normally buy, this is known as brand
explanation: Insistence. This is a very favorable situation for a manufacturer but difficult to achieve. Brand recognition is the stage of brand loyalty in which consumers are made aware of a brand's existence. Brand extension is the brand strategy of using successful brand names to introduce new products. In brand preference, consumers would rather buy a certain brand but will accept a substitute.

prompt: A customer service that allows a customer to buy a home entertainment system and use it before paying for it is called a __________ sale.
explanation: Charge. When customers buy on credit, they charge the merchandise to their accounts and pay for it later. Charge account customers are often favored by electronics retailers because a good debtor-creditor relationship tends to play a key role in maintaining customer relationships. COD sales occur when a customer pays for an item upon delivery. A cash sale occurs when customers pay for merchandise with money or the equivalent (check, money order, etc.). If an electronics retailer withdraws an item from stock and holds it in storage for a customer, this is a layaway sale.

prompt: Which of the following is a statement that is likely to be found in a small electronics company's brand promise:
choices: You have 30 days to return unwanted merchandise for a full refund.
Act now to receive a 20% discount on electronic appliances.
We are the only small electronics business in town that offers free delivery.
We will provide you with the best service possible.
explanation: We will provide you with the best service possible. A brand promise consists of three or four simple statements that describe what a small business will deliver to its customers. In this case, part of the overall promise is to deliver the best service possible. A refund policy is a very important customer service that is just one of the many things that a small electronics company does to deliver on its brand promise, including to deliver the best service possible. An offer to receive a 20% discount is a promotion meant to encourage a sale. While "We are the only small electronics business in town that offers free delivery" may be a fact, it is not a promise to deliver on the business's brand characteristics and values.

prompt: Special interest groups often use promotion in order to
explanation: Communicate ideas. Any organization that has something to sell uses promotion at one time or another. Special interest groups are communicating information about ideas rather than about products. They use promotion to communicate their ideas and encourage the public to accept those ideas. Special interest groups usually do not sell products or services. Their main goal is to promote a specific idea rather than to publicize their image.

prompt: Which of the following is an advantage of personal selling over advertising in the promotional mix:
explanation: Immediate feedback. In personal selling, the salesperson is able to learn immediately what the customer likes or dislikes about a product—whether the salesperson is helping the customer in person or over the telephone. This enables the salesperson to be flexible and to tailor the presentation to meet the needs of the particular customer. Personal selling is more costly on a per contact basis than advertising.

prompt: A business that sponsors a sweepstakes promotion and exaggerates the retail price of the grand prize is engaging in unethical behavior known as
explanation: Value misrepresentation. Value misrepresentation is unethical behavior because the advertiser is not being honest about the cost or value of the prize. For example, an organization provides a television set as a prize for a contest. The organization claims that the television is worth $500 but actually retails for $300 at an electronics store. Price discrimination occurs when businesses sell similar products to similar customers at different prices. Benefit exploitation is not a common term used to describe advertising practices, however, the term might be considered similar in meaning to puffery. Puffery is a tactic used by advertisers that exaggerates the positive attributes of a product. Cost fixation is not a term commonly used to describe advertising practices and should not be confused with price fixing.

prompt: Which of the following media could increase an appliance store's sales by reaching people who are driving home from work:
explanation: Radio. Radio can target customers at various times of the day such as when people are driving to or from work listening to their radios. Television would require that most customers already be at their homes. Newspapers are usually read either at work, or at home, but not usually by people driving in their cars. Direct mail would usually be read at home.

prompt: The part of a print advertisement that asks for action to take place is the
explanation: Copy. One purpose of print advertising copy is to ask the customer to buy. Much like a sales presentation, the ad will only create action if the copy uses words that induce action. Other purposes include sustaining the attention and interest created by the headline and/or illustration and building desire. The illustration is used to attract the reader's attention and to create interest. The logotype is a design or trademark used by the business for identification. The layout is the way in which the elements of an advertisement are arranged.

prompt: To obtain data about targeted prospects, the owner of a home security company might purchase mailing information from a
explanation: List broker. Businesses often use list brokers to obtain mailing lists for specific markets. The businesses use the lists to develop company databases that contain information about prospective customers. The broker acts as a liaison between the list owner and list buyer. Postal-exchange house, catalog bank, and requisition center are not terms that are commonly used to describe entities that arrange mailing list purchases.

prompt: When developing a sales packet for technical medical equipment, the sales representative might include
choices: a company catalog and the marketing budget.
product brochures and a signed contract.
user testimonials and a sample of the product.
explanation: Warranty information and product diagrams. The purpose of sales packets is to provide customers and prospects with information about products. Information such as price lists, price quotations, catalogs, testimonials, brochures, warranty information, and product diagrams are often included in sales packets. The materials that are included in sales packets are often determined by the nature of the product. For example, samples of hand lotion are easily distributed to customers, but it is not feasible to give customers samples of expensive medical equipment. Sales packets are generally distributed before the sale has been finalized. Therefore, signed contracts are usually not included in a sales packet.

prompt: Electronic products manufacturers that incorporate several environmentally-oriented objectives in the promotional plan usually emphasize __________ strategies.
explanation: Public relations. Public relations is a career that involves dealing with controversial public issues that are related to a company or its products. The primary goal of a business's public relations efforts is to create or enhance its image. To create a particular image, public relations departments might sponsor community events, support charitable organizations, or send newsletters to its various constituents. Environmental issues that directly relate to the business are often addressed. Direct mail is a form of advertising that comes to consumers' homes and businesses. Personal selling is a form of promotion that determines client needs and wants and responds through planned, personalized communication that influences purchase decisions and enhances future business opportunities. Cooperative advertising refers to the funds that businesses provide their customers to help pay for their customers' advertising expenses. Although direct mail, personal selling, and cooperative advertising are important elements in the promotional mix, these types of activities do not always address environmental issues.

prompt: Donna developed a unique new method for selling digital cameras. She is demonstrating her
explanation: Creativity. Creativity is the ability to generate unique ideas, approaches, solutions, etc. You need to be creative in your efforts to sell. Product knowledge is used to show the benefits of a product, self-confidence shows that you believe in your products, and communication skills involve expressing yourself clearly to your customers.

prompt: Which consumer regulation would protect a customer who purchased a vacuum cleaner from a door-to-door salesperson and wished to return it two days later?
explanation: State cooling-off laws. State cooling-off laws protect consumers by allowing them to cancel contracts with door-to-door salespeople within a certain number of days after the sale. The Uniform Commercial Credit Code provides the states with a model to follow in drawing up their sets of credit laws. The Truth-in-Lending Act requires finance charges to be disclosed. The Consumer Product Safety Act established the Consumer Product Safety Commission, giving it jurisdiction over the safety of the majority of consumer products.

prompt: One way that technical salespeople often are able to gain the trust and confidence of their customers is by
explanation: Behaving ethically. Ethics are the basic principles that govern a technical salesperson's behavior. Technical salespeople who are ethical treat customers fairly, present their goods and services truthfully, and provide as much information as possible. Ethical salespeople usually are able to gain the trust and confidence of their customers because the customers feel that the salespeople are being honest with them. As a result of their ethical behavior, technical salespeople often are able to develop long-term relationships with customers. Entertaining lavishly, lowering prices, and making promises they cannot keep are not ways of gaining a customer's trust and confidence.

prompt: How can technical salespeople convert complex terminology in written presentations into more simple, easy-to-understand language?
choices: Provide each of your customers with a dictionary, since they will need it often to explain complex terms.
Prospect only for those customers who can understand the most detailed, complicated concepts.
Always substitute one-syllable words for more technical terms, even if the meaning is changed somewhat.
Use short, simple words and sentences and include a glossary at the beginning.
explanation: Use short, simple words and sentences and include a glossary at the beginning. Technical salespeople must thoroughly know their audience and customers and be able to assess their levels of understanding. So that the audience understands complex concepts, the salesperson must tailor both oral and written presentations. By using short, simple words and sentences, a salesperson can enhance the audience's understanding of more complex concepts; and in written presentations, it is extremely helpful to customers to have a glossary of terms at the beginning, which allows the readers to become familiar with the technical terms. This provides a distinct advantage as they continue through the rest of the presentation. It is unwise and probably impossible to prospect only for customers who understand complex concepts. Most customers will not understand, and it is the job of the technical salesperson to help them understand in every way possible. Customers will appreciate the salesperson's extra effort because these types of efforts contribute to building a positive relationship with the customer. Providing customers with dictionaries communicates to them that the burden of understanding is on them. Instead, technical salespeople want to convey to customers that they (salespeople) will do everything they can to help customers understand the technical aspects of the product. While written presentations should be as simple and direct as possible, it would be incorrect to substitute words that do not convey the correct meaning. Simplicity should not take priority over accuracy; the two should work hand-in-hand.

prompt: One of the purposes of establishing a relationship with a customer in the beginning of the technical selling process is to
explanation: Gain the customer's confidence. The completion of the sale may be determined by the first few minutes that a technical salesperson spends with the customer. The technical salesperson's goals should include gaining a repeat customer, not simply closing one sale. In order to do that, the technical salesperson should attempt to help the customer feel comfortable, not on guard. Technical salespeople should welcome customer objections because they indicate the customer's interest in the product.

prompt: An effective approach to opening a sale should include words and actions that are
choices: used only if a customer shows interest.
relative to a customer's age and appearance.
explanation: Sincere and friendly. Customers should sense that you are sincerely interested in helping to satisfy their buying needs. To convey this attitude, you must approach the customer in a sincere and friendly manner. Avoid stereotyping customers on the basis of age and appearance because this can limit your opportunities to successfully sell. Because every customer is different, it is important to recognize their individual needs and tailor your approach to them. The timing of your approach is important, and each customer should feel welcome and important—even if they aren't interested in buying right away.

prompt: Which of the following is an important purpose of questioning a customer:
explanation: To identify the customer's needs. Questions help the salesperson to discover the customer's needs and buying motives, which in turn helps the salesperson to offer products that will meet those needs. Questions about personal matters or credit should not be asked. Neither should the salesperson question the customer in order to promote a personal relationship.

prompt: Technical salespeople can gain the respect of their customers by exhibiting
explanation: Self-confidence. Self-confidence is confidence in oneself and in one's abilities. Technical salespeople who exhibit a certain amount of self-confidence usually are able to gain the respect and confidence of their customers. Customers often are more willing to buy from technical salespeople who act sure of themselves and of the goods and services they are selling. Self-discipline is training yourself to act in ways that will further your development. Self-reliance is relying on your own efforts and abilities. Self-importance is overestimating one's importance.

prompt: A physical characteristic of a digital camera is known as a(n)
explanation: Feature. A feature is a specific factor that can be seen, felt, heard, smelled, or tasted. A feature helps to describe a product such as a digital camera. A benefit is the gain or satisfaction a buyer receives from a product. Image refers to the way that customers view something. Style refers to the overall look or appearance of a product.

prompt: In technical selling, an objection from the customer is considered a(n)
explanation: Point of difference. When a potential customer/client raises an objection, s/he is expressing a question or concern over some aspect of the good or service. It can be viewed as a point of difference in that the customer does not agree with the point being made by the technical salesperson. An objection should never be allowed to degenerate into an argument, as both parties lose in an argumentative situation. An objection should not be viewed as a refusal to purchase, since objections frequently are indications of customer interest and the need for additional selling effort. Objections are natural to the technical selling process and are not an indication of a salesperson's mistakes.

prompt: A guideline that an electronics salesperson can use to close the sale for a plasma television is to choose the closing method that
explanation: Fits the sales situation. The closing technique chosen should be suited to the circumstances, not selected on the basis of whether it is easy to use or frequently used. Each customer and each product is different, so there is no one recommended way to handle all closes. Closing on objection is a closing technique in which an electronics salesperson answers a customer's objection so that the customer no longer has a reason not to buy. It is only appropriate when customers raise objections.

prompt: Why is it important for technical salespeople to watch customers' body language and look for feedback?
choices: To make sure customers understand the sales message
To find out if customers have the funds to pay
To sell aggressively when customers begin to complain
To exaggerate benefits if customers seem hesitant
explanation: To make sure customers understand the sales message. Technical salespeople should watch for signs that customers understand the sales message and are reacting favorably. To do this, it is helpful to watch the body language, which is the gestures, facial expression, tone of voice, or any other form of communicating without words. Body language that indicates understanding and acceptance includes leaning forward, smiling, nodding, and making eye contact. This is a type of feedback that indicates how customers feel about the sales message. Depending on the feedback, salespeople can make adjustments to the presentation to increase the possibility of a sale. Salespeople do not watch body language and look for feedback to find out if customers have the funds to pay. Salespeople should never sell aggressively or exaggerate the benefits of a product.

prompt: Good technical salespeople know that their selling efforts should include follow-up
choices: only after they make a sale.
whether or not they make a sale.
if customers give them repeat business.
in order to promote cognitive dissonance.
explanation: Whether or not they make a sale. Successful technical salespeople use follow-up whether or not they make a sale. If they didn't make a sale, they want to determine why not and whether the customer's needs or wants have changed. The use of follow-up is not based on whether customers give repeat business, but follow-up may lead to repeat business. Technical salespeople try to combat cognitive dissonance, not promote it, as it refers to an individual's post-purchase anxiety.

prompt: Manually calculate the amount of sales tax for the following situation: A customer purchases three DVD players that cost $74.95 each. The sales tax rate is 12%.
explanation: $26.98. To calculate the amount of sales tax on three DVD players that cost $74.95 each, first determine the total cost for all three DVD players: $74.95 x 3 = $224.85. Then, convert the percentage of sales tax into a decimal figure, and multiply the total cost by that decimal figure. For this situation: $224.85 x 12% = $224.85 x .12 = $26.98. It is not necessary to round up since the third number after the decimal is less than five.

prompt: What is the amount of change that an electronics salesperson owes a customer if the customer tenders a $100 bill for a special-order item that costs $130, but the customer paid a 50% deposit at the time of order and there is a $15 handling charge and sales tax of 6%?
explanation: $11.30. First, calculate the total cost by adding the price of the item and the handling charge ($130 + $15 = $145). Then, calculate the sales tax by multiplying the total price by the amount of tax ($145 x 6% or .06 = $8.70). Add the tax to the total price ($145.00 + $8.70 = $153.70). The customer paid a 50% deposit on the price of the item, which amounts to $65 ($130 x 50% or .50 = $65). Subtract the deposit from the total cost to determine the remaining amount due ($153.70 - $65.00 = $88.70). If the customer tenders a $100-bill, subtract the amount due to determine the charge ($100.00 - $88.70 = $11.30).

prompt: What piece of equipment would an electronics store cashier use to confirm that a customer has been approved to charge the amount of a sale?
explanation: Electronic credit authorizer. To confirm that a customer has been approved to charge the amount of a sale, most businesses use electronic credit authorizers. These devices transmit customer information to the issuer of the credit card and receive approval or denial in a matter of seconds. Mechanical imprinters are used to imprint customer information onto a credit card sales check. Interactive computer systems allow customers to access information about a business or a product. Digital scanners are used to copy data and graphics and input them into a computer.

prompt: A customer calls and requests cable installation. What is the most important information that the service employee obtains from the customer?
choices: Street number, zip code, and fax number
Telephone number, street address, and name
Name, e-mail address, and telephone number
Mailing address, fax number, and street address
explanation: Telephone number, street address, and name. To install television cable service, a service person must obtain entrance to the property of the individual requesting service. To complete the transaction, the minimal amount of information needed is the name of the person requesting service, the street address of the location, and a telephone number to reach the service requestor. Although a fax number and e-mail address are helpful, the information is not necessary. A mailing address is often a post office box. Without the street name and number, the service person does not know where to go. A zip code is helpful but does not provide the exact location of the property where the cable installation is to occur.

prompt: Which of the following is the most appropriate method for an video rental and electronic games store to use to prospect for customers:
choices: Change its promotional mix on a regular basis
Make cold calls to newcomers in the community
Place flyers on automobile windshields of customers parked in the store's parking lot
Enclose a gift certificate in newcomers' packets given out by the local chamber of commerce
explanation: Enclose a gift certificate in newcomers' packets given out by the local chamber of commerce. Video rental and electronic games stores do not prospect like other businesses. One way of contacting new people to shop in a video rental and electronics games store is to include gift certificates in the newcomers' packets that will encourage them to visit the business. Placing flyers on cars in the store's parking lot will reach existing customers. Video rental and electronics games stores do not make cold calls to new customers. Regularly changing the promotional mix might confuse existing customers as well as potential new customers.

prompt: What is often an effective way to begin a sales letter?
explanation: Ask a question. Sales letters need to gain the customers' attention quickly and keep them interested. One way to get attention is to begin the letter by asking a question. The question should be relevant to customers and one that they probably want answered, such as, "Do you want to save 30% in expenses next year?" Sales letters usually do not begin by correcting a misunderstanding, saying thank-you, or congratulating an associate.

prompt: One method that businesses use to motivate technical salespeople to increase their sales is
explanation: Holding a sales convention. At sales conventions, technical salespeople are exposed to motivational speakers, as well as meeting peers who have the same problems, concerns, and challenges. Estimating sales-unit potential is part of a process in establishing sales territories. Promotional and buying allowances are forms of sales promotion used to stimulate a wholesaler or retailer to purchase items but not to motivate technical salespeople.

prompt: In order to develop effective selling strategies for their businesses, sales managers must
choices: focus their efforts on controlling sales activity.
understand the nature of their customers' businesses.
motivate their customers to purchase high-end products.
create an organized and rigid work environment for sales staff.
explanation: Understand the nature of their customers' businesses. Sales managers are often responsible for developing and implementing optimal selling strategies and programs. When determining appropriate and effective strategies, the sales manager must understand the target market. For example, an office supply distributor might need to employ different selling strategies than a retailer because the target markets are very different (organizational vs. consumer). Generally, the salespeople motivate customers to buy products, and the sales managers motivate the salespeople to sell the products. Effective sales managers should create an organized but flexible working environment. Some flexibility is often helpful when working with sales staff members who have different personalities, skills, and experiences. Contemporary sales managers should balance their efforts by acting as a coach, mentor, supervisor, and motivator for sales personnel.

prompt: Why do technical salespeople follow a route plan when calling on customers?
choices: To eliminate the risk of unexpected travel delays and expenses
To call on the maximum number of customers with the least amount of travel time
To increase travel time when calling on established customers and prospects
To reduce the need for telephone follow-up with customers
explanation: To call on the maximum number of customers with the least amount of travel time. The sales staff's goal is to generate as many sales as possible. To do that, they must call on as many customers as they can in a given time period. To save time and money, it is best to call on several customers that are relatively close in proximity. Following a route plan does not necessarily reduce the need for telephone follow-up, nor does it reduce the risk of unexpected delays or expenses. The goal is to decrease travel time, not increase it.

prompt: When assigning business equipment salespeople to territories, sales managers should keep in mind the need to
explanation: Balance workloads. When assigning business equipment salespeople to territories, sales managers usually analyze the amount of work that is necessary to cover the area. The goal is to make the workload as equal as possible among all business equipment salespeople. Businesses do not want to give one salesperson a substantially heavier workload than others. To avoid doing that, it may be necessary to divide one territory between two business equipment salespeople. Sales managers try to minimize selling costs, establish sales areas of reasonable size, and reduce travel expenses.

prompt: Before establishing prospecting standards, technical sales managers often develop a
explanation: Market analysis. To increase sales, technical companies first need to evaluate how their products are currently being used and where the products have potential use. By conducting a study or analyzing different market segments, technical sales managers can identify new target markets for their products. Once the markets are determined, sales managers can use the information to establish appropriate criteria to qualify prospects. A customer profile is maintained by sales representatives and documents detailed information including contacts, key decision makers, and sales history. A sales report is a summary of various sales information and is collected for many purposes. For example, sales reports are often used to flag slow-moving products or a salesperson's activities. Cold calls are unannounced visits by a salesperson to prospects about whom little may be known. A cold-call summary is a report that records a salesperson's activities in regard to cold calling.

prompt: UltraTech Electronic Games is getting ready to distribute its latest interactive gaming device and must train the company's sales personnel. The primary objective of the training process is to
explanation: Introduce new products. Sales training is the systematic process for enabling salespeople to acquire the attitudes, knowledge, and skills that are needed in order to attain organizational goals. When developing a training program, a technical business must determine the purpose or objective of the training in order to develop appropriate training activities. Many technical businesses develop training programs that incorporate various related goals. UltraTech's primary training objective is to introduce a new product to the salespeople so that they are better prepared to sell the new gaming device when it is ready to go on the market. Product information and training helps facilitate this goal. Improving teamwork efforts, assigning new sales territories, and informing salespeople about ethical policies are valid objectives for sales training; however, they are not primary objectives for UltraTech Electronic Games.

prompt: A computer parts business that assigns salespeople to call on customers in a five-state area surrounding their home base is establishing sales territories on a __________ basis.
explanation: Geographic. Dividing the country into geographic units is one way of establishing sales territories. A state is a common geographic unit that is easy to identify. For example, a business might have a salesperson in Ohio who is responsible for servicing the surrounding states of Pennsylvania, West Virginia, Kentucky, Indiana, and Michigan. The advantage of this method is that one salesperson may be able to easily travel throughout the area and handle the needs of customers within that area. A localized sales territory would not include several states. A territory based on population would consider the number of people in an area. A national territory would cover the entire country.

prompt: A plant manager or a department head would be an example of which level of management?
explanation: Middle. This level of management is responsible for the daily functioning of the business. It also serves as a liaison between top-level and supervisory management. Top management develops broad company plans, while supervisory, or operating, management is the management level that implements management plans through direct supervision of workers.

prompt: The first step in the control process that management should follow to determine if the company is achieving planned annual sales and profits is to
choices: set monthly or quarterly sales and profit goals.
determine causes of lagging sales or profits
explanation: Set monthly or quarterly sales and profit goals. The first step is to set monthly or quarterly goals that will give management a yardstick by which to measure performance. The alternatives are the other steps in the control process that occur later. These steps cannot be carried out until the goals are set.
